segments.text: Here we are.
The tower in front of you is the Torre del Soccorso.
And the wall running up the hill to the Rocca, the fortress, is the Camminamento del Soccorso, a fortified walkway.
Now, this is my work.
The tower, the passage and the Rocca form a single defensive system.
A machine built of stone.
The name Soccorso means relief. That tells you what it was for.
Imagine Vicopisano under attack.
The enemy enters the town, occupies the streets and forces the soldiers to retreat into the Rocca.
A rather unpleasant situation, especially for those inside.
But even then, this route remained.
Men, food and supplies could come in from outside through the bottom of the tower, reach the protected walkway and make their way up to the Rocca.
All without crossing streets controlled by the enemy.
That's why this isn't just a wall.
It's a protected route, designed to remain usable when all the other routes were no longer safe.
When I arrived in Vicopisano, I asked myself a question.
What could go wrong?
A siege, enemies entering the town, or the Rocca being cut off.
And in each case, what could the defenders do?
The Camminamento del Soccorso grew out of questions like these.
It even had to work if the town rebelled and the Florentine garrison was forced to withdraw into the Rocca.
Florence had only recently conquered Vicopisano, and trust was not exactly the most plentiful material in a newly occupied territory.
And I must admit, I've never been much of an expert in either trust or politics.
So I preferred to rely on stone.
Today, you can walk along the passage with rather more peace of mind.
No armour, no supplies on your back and, above all, nobody trying to conquer the town.
Now, let's head towards the town centre.
Our next stop will be Palazzo Pretorio.
